title: Wanting, being able and needing to act
summary: Use vouloir, pouvoir and devoir with an infinitive; distinguish obligation from a need and express purpose with pour.
objectives: Conjugate vouloir, pouvoir and devoir in every present person.
Keep a second verb in the infinitive.
Distinguish devoir, avoir besoin de and pour + infinitive.

sections.title: Conjugate the first verb; leave the action in its dictionary form
paragraphs: Vouloir means want, pouvoir means can or be able to, and devoir commonly means must or have to. When they introduce another action, the second verb stays in the infinitive. Do not insert à or de after these three verbs in this construction. Pouvoir can express permission as well as ability or possibility.
Learn all the forms below. Je peux is the ordinary present of pouvoir; je puis is a more formal alternative, especially in Puis-je… ? requests. This lesson practises peux in ordinary statements.
points: Je veux partir = I want to leave; je peux partir = I can leave; je dois partir = I must leave.

mistakes.why: Only the first verb is conjugated.

sections.title: An obligation and a need can overlap without being identical
paragraphs: Devoir + infinitive usually presents something as required: je dois partir can mean I have to leave. Avoir besoin de + noun or infinitive presents a need: j'ai besoin de repos (I need rest), j'ai besoin de dormir (I need to sleep). A personal need is not necessarily an external obligation, but both can translate English need to in context. De becomes d' before a vowel. Do not attach de to devoir just because besoin uses it.
points: Le repos (m.) means rest. Besoin is part of a fixed avoir expression.

examples.english: I have to leave at eight o'clock.

sections.title: Pour + infinitive explains the purpose of an action
paragraphs: Use pour + infinitive for in order to when the understood doer of that infinitive is the same as the main subject. Je travaille pour payer means I work in order to pay. This is different from vouloir: one states a purpose, the other a desire. A separate subject after pour requires a different construction, taught later.
points: Do not conjugate the verb immediately after purpose pour.

examples.french: Je prends le bus **pour aller** au travail.
examples.english: I take the bus to get to work.
examples.note: The same person takes the bus and goes to work.

examples.english: We work to pay the rent.

mistakes.avoid: Je travaille pour je paie le loyer.
mistakes.prefer: Je travaille pour payer le loyer.
mistakes.why: With the same understood subject, pour takes the infinitive.

practice.prompt: Use the dictionary form of étudier: 'Je viens pour ___.'

practice.explanation: The plural third person uses veulent.

practice.prompt: Correct only the second verb: 'Il peut entre.' Write the sentence.
practice.explanation: The second verb stays in the infinitive.

practice.prompt: Complete with de or no preposition. Write de or aucun: 'Je dois ___ travailler.'
Supply the missing preposition: 'J'ai besoin ___ repos.'
practice.explanation: Avoir besoin de introduces a noun or infinitive.

practice.prompt: Which wording explicitly presents sleeping as a personal need?
practice.explanation: Pouvoir expresses ability or permission; besoin expresses a need.

practice.prompt: Join using pour and the infinitive, keeping the first clause: 'Nous venons. Nous voulons apprendre.' Write 'Nous venons ___.'
practice.explanation: Pour apprendre supplies the purpose with the same subject.

practice.prompt: Supply de with any required elision: 'J'ai besoin ___ apprendre.'
practice.explanation: De becomes d' before a vowel.

production_task.prompt: Explain a study plan: one thing you want to do, one obligation, and the purpose of your study using pour.
production_task.model_answer: Je veux apprendre le français. Je dois travailler ce soir. J'étudie le matin pour préparer mon examen.
production_task.translation: I want to learn French. I have to work this evening. I study in the morning to prepare for my exam.
rubric: Conjugate the first verb but not the following infinitive.
Use pour + infinitive for the same person's purpose.
